back: Production targets for the whole economy over five years, set by Gosplan; the first began in 1928.
Joining peasant farms into large state-controlled collective farms (kolkhozy), from 1929.
A better-off peasant; the label used for peasants who resisted collectivisation.
A worker who greatly exceeded targets, named after the miner Alexei Stakhanov (1935).

front: Name two great projects of the Five-Year Plans.
back: Magnitogorsk (iron and steel city) and the Dnieper dam (1932); also the Moscow Metro (1935).

front: What happened to livestock during collectivisation?
back: Numbers fell by about half as peasants slaughtered animals rather than hand them over.

front: How many died in the famine of 1932-33 (estimates)?
back: Historians estimate about 5-7 million across the USSR, especially in Ukraine and Kazakhstan.

front: What was the 'double burden' of Soviet women?
back: Full-time paid work plus nearly all the housework and childcare.

front: Were Stalin's economic policies a success?
back: Industry and military power grew fast, but at huge human cost: famine, deportation, low living standards.
